Three representations of methane
The space-filling, structural, and ball-and-stick drawings are shown side by side, matching the textbook comparison.
C–H bond length remains 109 pm for every bond.

elements: three-panel row composition showing the same methane molecule simultaneously: space-filling model on the left, structural drawing in the center, ball-and-stick model on the right
left panel space-filling model: dark gray central carbon van der Waals sphere mostly hidden between the hydrogens
left panel space-filling model: four large warm off-white hydrogen van der Waals spheres arranged tetrahedrally around carbon and overlapping/touching so they crowd the carbon
left panel space-filling model: glossy shading and soft contact/overlap regions suggesting filled molecular volume
center panel structural drawing: flat front-facing black text label C at the center
center panel structural drawing: flat front-facing black text label H directly above C
center panel structural drawing: flat front-facing black text label H to the lower-left/left of C
center panel structural drawing: flat front-facing black text label H to the right of C
center panel structural drawing: flat front-facing black text label H below and slightly right of C
center panel structural drawing: thin black plain bond line from C vertically upward to the top H
center panel structural drawing: thin black plain bond line from C down-left to the left H
center panel structural drawing: thin black plain bond line from C slightly down-right to the right H
center panel structural drawing: heavy solid black wedge bond slanting down-right from C to the lower H, narrow at carbon and broad at hydrogen
center panel structural drawing: magenta dashed extension ray continuing the upward C-H bond beyond the top H
center panel structural drawing: magenta dashed extension ray continuing the left-hand C-H bond outward beyond the left H
center panel structural drawing: magenta double-headed curved arrow sweeping around the upper-left side between the upward and left-hand bond-extension rays
center panel structural drawing: magenta text label Bond angle 109.5º near the curved arrow
center panel structural drawing: upper magenta dashed horizontal guide line extending rightward from the top H level
center panel structural drawing: lower magenta dashed horizontal guide line extending rightward from the carbon level
center panel structural drawing: magenta vertical double-headed arrow between the two horizontal guide lines
center panel structural drawing: magenta text label Bond length 109 pm to the right of the vertical double arrow
right panel ball-and-stick model: dark gray central carbon sphere
right panel ball-and-stick model: four smaller warm off-white hydrogen spheres at tetrahedral positions around carbon
right panel ball-and-stick model: four thin pale blue cylindrical C-H rods connecting carbon to each hydrogen
subtle hover/click highlight rings or glows that can appear on corresponding carbon, hydrogen, or C-H bond elements across all three panels

interactions.label: Focus representation
interactions.teaches: The learner compares three simultaneous depictions of one methane molecule: occupied volume, measured structural formula, and open tetrahedral connectivity are different views of the same CH4 geometry

Clicking an atom or C-H bond shows its counterpart in all three panels, making clear that the labeled length and angle in the structural drawing belong to the same tetrahedral molecule shown by the two 3D models

Rotating the two molecular models reveals that methane is not planar: the four equivalent C-H bonds point toward the corners of a tetrahedron while the central structural diagram remains a flat measurement drawing

demo_steps.title: Compare all three representations
demo_steps.narration: All three panels are visible at once, matching the textbook layout. The same methane molecule is shown as filled atomic volume, as a measured structural drawing, and as an open ball-and-stick model.

demo_steps.title: Read the measurements
demo_steps.narration: Focusing the center panel keeps the structural formula front-on and flat. The magenta arc marks the H-C-H bond angle of 109.5º, and the magenta guide arrow marks the C-H bond length of 109 pm.

demo_steps.title: Connect the drawing to the 3D skeleton
demo_steps.narration: The ball-and-stick model exposes the four C-H rods radiating from carbon. It shows that the measured angle in the structural drawing is a projection of a tetrahedral three-dimensional arrangement.

demo_steps.title: Connect the skeleton to molecular volume
demo_steps.narration: The space-filling model shows why carbon is barely visible: the four hydrogen spheres crowd around it. The same tetrahedral positions now appear as occupied atomic volume rather than rods and labels.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a single front-facing three-panel composition with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z toward the viewer. Use a weak-perspective or nearly orthographic camera so the center structural formula is not tilted. Overall scene spans about X = -5.8 to +5.8 and Y = -1.8 to +1.8. Panel centers: space-filling at X = -3.9, structural drawing at X = 0, ball-and-stick at X = +3.9. Keep all three panels visible by default. Methane C-H bond length is 109 pm; map this to 1.09 world units from carbon center to each hydrogen center in the ball-and-stick model and to about 1.05 world units in the structural drawing. Use tetrahedral direction vectors approximately normalized from carbon: top/back H = (0, 1.02, -0.38), left/back H = (-0.94, -0.37, -0.38), right/back H = (0.94, -0.24, -0.44), lower/front H = (0.28, -0.86, 0.64), each scaled to radius 1.09. This gives a readable front view with the lower/front bond slanting down-right. Left space-filling model: carbon sphere radius about 0.58, color dark gray #4b5555; hydrogen spheres radius about 0.72, warm off-white #d8d6bd. Place the four hydrogen sphere centers using the same tetrahedral directions but slightly compressed to bond-center distance 0.92 so the spheres visibly overlap/touch and the carbon is mostly hidden between them. Right ball-and-stick model: carbon sphere radius 0.28, hydrogen sphere radius 0.20, rods radius 0.045, rod color pale blue #9ec2df, carbon #4b5555, hydrogens #d8d6bd. Center structural drawing must be a flat XY diagram at Z = 0 and billboard/front-facing at all times. Structural C at (0, 0). Top H at (0, 1.08). Left H at (-1.02, -0.40). Right H at (1.04, -0.18). Lower wedge H at (0.34, -1.02). Plain black bonds #111111: C to top H vertical, C to left H down-left, C to right H slightly down-right. Wedge bond: filled black triangle with apex/narrow end at carbon, centerline from C to (0.34, -1.02), length about 0.95, broad end width about 0.28 near the lower H; it must visibly slant down-right, not straight down. Magenta annotation color #d81b8c or #ff1493. Bond-angle dashed extension ray for upward bond: vertical magenta dashed line from just above C through the top H and continuing upward, approximately x = 0, y = 0.45 to 1.55. Bond-angle dashed extension ray for left bond: magenta dashed line collinear with C-to-left-H bond, running from about (-0.38, -0.15) through the left H and outward to about (-1.45, -0.57). Curved double-headed arc: center near C, radius about 0.62, sweep on the upper-left/outside of the bonds from roughly 92 degrees to 202 degrees in screen coordinates, with arrowheads tangent to the arc at both ends. Place label 'Bond angle 109.5º' above-left of carbon around x = -0.82, y = 0.86. Bond-length guide lines: magenta dashed horizontal guides run rightward from top H level y = 1.08 and carbon level y = 0.00, starting just right of the vertical bond around x = 0.18 and ending near x = 1.72. Vertical double-headed magenta arrow at x = 1.72 from y = 0.00 to y = 1.08. Place text 'Bond length 109 pm' to the right at about x = 1.96, y = 0.54. FocusRepresentation should dim, outline, or slightly brighten the chosen panel, but should not replace the three-panel layout in the default view.
plan.notes: Render the central structural panel as screen-aligned 2D text, line, dashed-line, and filled-triangle geometry in an overlay-like group that remains front-on even when orbiting. Orbit3dModels should affect only the left and right molecular model groups, or should leave the center structural group billboarded and fixed so it never tilts in perspective. Use smooth sphere geometry with high specular highlights for the molecular models. For the space-filling panel, allow true sphere overlap and use soft lighting/ambient occlusion to make the central carbon barely visible through gaps; do not make the hydrogens transparent unless necessary. For the focus toggle, keep all three panels present; non-focused panels can be desaturated or dimmed to about 30 percent opacity rather than hidden. For click correspondence, picking any H or C-H bond should add a magenta or cyan highlight to the matching atom/bond in the other two panels, including a small glow or outline on the relevant structural label/line.

authoredPrompt: This figure renders a single methane molecule three ways in one row, moving from a solid-volume picture to a measured structural drawing to an open skeleton. At the left is a space-filling model in which four large off-white hydrogen spheres crowd around a dark gray carbon that is barely visible between them, the spheres touching and flattening against one another. In the center is a structural drawing: the central "C" joins an "H" directly above, an "H" at the left, and an "H" at the right by plain black lines, and a fourth "H" below by a heavy black wedge. A magenta double-headed curved arrow sweeps between two dashed magenta rays that extend the upward and left-hand bonds, labeled "Bond angle 109.5º". Short magenta dashed lines run rightward from the upper hydrogen and from the carbon to a vertical double arrow labeled "Bond length 109 pm". At the right is a ball-and-stick model with the dark gray carbon at the center and four pale hydrogen spheres held out on thin pale blue rods. Showing one molecule in three styles lets the reader attach the two measurements to a shape also seen as filled volume, fixing the tetrahedral geometry that results when four equivalent hybrid orbitals on carbon overlap with hydrogen orbitals.
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle representation style: space-filling, structural, and ball-and-stick views highlight the same methane molecule, showing how each representation emphasizes size, angles, or connectivity.
- Slider for dragging one hydrogen around the carbon; the structural drawing and model morph while the bond-angle readout updates toward 109.5 degrees, making the connection between four equivalent C-H bonds and tetrahedral spacing visible.
authoredContext:
When each of the four identical sp3 hybrid orbitals of a carbon atom overlaps with the 1s orbital of a hydrogen atom, four identical C–H bonds are formed and methane results. Each C–H bond in methane has a strength of 439 kJ/mol (105 kcal/mol) and a length of 109 pm. Because the four bonds have a specific geometry, we also can define a property called the bond angle. The angle formed by each H–C–H is 109.5°, the so-called tetrahedral angle. Methane thus has the structure shown in the figure.

The structure of methane, showing its 109.5° bond angles.

The space-filling model, wedge-dash structure, and ball and stick model of methane. The bond length between C-H is 109 pm, and the bond angle of H-C-H is 109.5 degrees.

interactions.label: Representation
interactions.teaches: The same tetrahedral methane geometry can emphasize different ideas: occupied volume in the space-filling model, measured angles and lengths in the structural drawing, and atom connectivity in the ball-and-stick model

interactions.label: Move one H: H-C-H angle
interactions.teaches: Four equivalent C-H bonds are most evenly separated at the tetrahedral angle of about 109.5°, so moving one hydrogen away from that value visibly distorts the symmetric methane shape
Rotating the model reveals that the four C-H bonds are not planar; they point toward the corners of a tetrahedron in three dimensions

demo_steps.title: Structural measurement
demo_steps.narration: The flat structural drawing labels the central carbon and four hydrogens while the magenta arc reads the H-C-H bond angle. At the ideal tetrahedral setting the readout is 109.5° and each C-H bond is labeled 109 pm.

demo_steps.title: Connectivity view
demo_steps.narration: Switch to ball-and-stick to see the same four hydrogens held away from carbon by four equivalent C-H bonds. The open rods make the tetrahedral connectivity and nonplanar spacing easy to see.

demo_steps.title: Occupied-volume view
demo_steps.narration: Switch to space-filling to see why the hydrogens crowd around carbon: the van der Waals spheres nearly hide the central carbon. The tetrahedral arrangement is the same, but the emphasis is molecular volume.

demo_steps.title: Distort one hydrogen
demo_steps.narration: Move one hydrogen to reduce the H-C-H angle. The readout drops below 109.5° and the molecule loses the even tetrahedral spacing of four equivalent C-H bonds.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use one methane molecule at the origin. C-H bond length is 109 pm; map this to 1.09 world units from carbon center to each hydrogen center. Ideal tetrahedral directions may be normalized vectors approximately: top/back H = (0, 1.03, -0.36), left/front H = (-0.89, -0.51, -0.36), right/front H = (0.89, -0.51, -0.36), lower/front H = (0, -0.25, 1.06), each scaled to radius 1.09 from carbon. The measured angle should be the angle between the top/back C-H vector and the selected movable left/front C-H vector; default 109.5°. The slider should rotate the selected left/front hydrogen in the plane spanned by its ideal vector and the top/back vector while keeping C-H length fixed at 1.09 world units. Space-filling radii: carbon van der Waals radius about 0.70 world units, hydrogen about 0.55 world units, causing visible overlap/contact; carbon dark gray #4b5555, hydrogen warm off-white #d9d8bd with glossy highlights. Ball-and-stick radii: carbon sphere 0.28, hydrogen spheres 0.18, rods radius 0.045; rods pale blue #9ec2df. Structural view should be rendered as a flat front-facing overlay in the XY plane: central C at (0,0), top H at (0,1.09), left H near (-0.95,-0.40), right H near (0.95,-0.20), lower/front H near (0.25,-0.95). Plain bonds are thin black lines #111111, wedge bond is a filled tapered black triangle from C toward lower/front H. Magenta measurement annotations use #ff1493. Place 'Bond angle 109.5°' above-left of carbon, curved arrow sweeping from the upward bond extension to the left bond extension. Place bond-length guide lines to the right of the upper bond and carbon with vertical double arrow and text 'Bond length 109 pm'.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the three representation styles as separate visibility groups sharing the same underlying atom positions so the slider morphs every style consistently. In Structural mode, keep the drawing mostly front-facing like the source figure and update the left H label, its bond line, dashed extension ray, magenta angle arc, and numeric angle readout. In Space-filling mode use transparent or slightly clipped overlaps only if needed so the dark carbon remains faintly visible between hydrogens, matching the source. In Ball-and-stick mode use smooth spheres with Phong/standard material, strong white specular highlights, and cylinders aligned along each C-H vector. Orbit should be enabled primarily for the 3D styles but may leave the structural labels billboarded toward the camera.

discrepancies: The ball-and-stick methane model is too flat and cross-like compared with the reference's tilted tetrahedral 3D arrangement.
The structural formula's right-side C-H bond appears as a plain solid bond rather than the dashed/back bond shown in the source.
The space-filling model has a noticeably different orientation and exposes the dark carbon differently than the reference.
The central structural diagram is visually larger and more dominant relative to the two molecular models than in the source.
The bond-length dashed guide geometry is not quite aligned like the source, especially the lower guide to the right hydrogen.

interactions.label: Focus representation
interactions.teaches: The learner compares three simultaneous depictions of one methane molecule: occupied volume, measured structural formula, and open tetrahedral connectivity are different views of the same CH4 geometry

Clicking an atom or C-H bond shows its counterpart in all three panels, making clear that the labeled length and angle in the structural drawing belong to the same tetrahedral molecule shown by the two 3D models

Rotating the two molecular models reveals that methane is not planar: the four equivalent C-H bonds point toward the corners of a tetrahedron while the central structural diagram remains a flat measurement drawing

demo_steps.title: Compare all three representations
demo_steps.narration: All three panels are visible at once, matching the textbook layout. The same methane molecule is shown as filled atomic volume, as a measured structural drawing, and as an open ball-and-stick model.

demo_steps.title: Read the measurements
demo_steps.narration: Focusing the center panel keeps the structural formula front-on and flat. The magenta arc marks the H-C-H bond angle of 109.5º, and the magenta guide arrow marks the C-H bond length of 109 pm.

demo_steps.title: Connect the drawing to the 3D skeleton
demo_steps.narration: The ball-and-stick model exposes the four C-H rods radiating from carbon. It shows that the measured angle in the structural drawing is a projection of a tetrahedral three-dimensional arrangement.

demo_steps.title: Connect the skeleton to molecular volume
demo_steps.narration: The space-filling model shows why carbon is barely visible: the four hydrogen spheres crowd around it. The same tetrahedral positions now appear as occupied atomic volume rather than rods and labels.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a single front-facing three-panel composition with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z toward the viewer. Use a weak-perspective or nearly orthographic camera so the center structural formula is not tilted. Overall scene spans about X = -5.8 to +5.8 and Y = -1.8 to +1.8. Panel centers: space-filling at X = -3.9, structural drawing at X = 0, ball-and-stick at X = +3.9. Keep all three panels visible by default. Methane C-H bond length is 109 pm; map this to 1.09 world units from carbon center to each hydrogen center in the ball-and-stick model and to about 1.05 world units in the structural drawing. Use tetrahedral direction vectors approximately normalized from carbon: top/back H = (0, 1.02, -0.38), left/back H = (-0.94, -0.37, -0.38), right/back H = (0.94, -0.24, -0.44), lower/front H = (0.28, -0.86, 0.64), each scaled to radius 1.09. This gives a readable front view with the lower/front bond slanting down-right. Left space-filling model: carbon sphere radius about 0.58, color dark gray #4b5555; hydrogen spheres radius about 0.72, warm off-white #d8d6bd. Place the four hydrogen sphere centers using the same tetrahedral directions but slightly compressed to bond-center distance 0.92 so the spheres visibly overlap/touch and the carbon is mostly hidden between them. Right ball-and-stick model: carbon sphere radius 0.28, hydrogen sphere radius 0.20, rods radius 0.045, rod color pale blue #9ec2df, carbon #4b5555, hydrogens #d8d6bd. Center structural drawing must be a flat XY diagram at Z = 0 and billboard/front-facing at all times. Structural C at (0, 0). Top H at (0, 1.08). Left H at (-1.02, -0.40). Right H at (1.04, -0.18). Lower wedge H at (0.34, -1.02). Plain black bonds #111111: C to top H vertical, C to left H down-left, C to right H slightly down-right. Wedge bond: filled black triangle with apex/narrow end at carbon, centerline from C to (0.34, -1.02), length about 0.95, broad end width about 0.28 near the lower H; it must visibly slant down-right, not straight down. Magenta annotation color #d81b8c or #ff1493. Bond-angle dashed extension ray for upward bond: vertical magenta dashed line from just above C through the top H and continuing upward, approximately x = 0, y = 0.45 to 1.55. Bond-angle dashed extension ray for left bond: magenta dashed line collinear with C-to-left-H bond, running from about (-0.38, -0.15) through the left H and outward to about (-1.45, -0.57). Curved double-headed arc: center near C, radius about 0.62, sweep on the upper-left/outside of the bonds from roughly 92 degrees to 202 degrees in screen coordinates, with arrowheads tangent to the arc at both ends. Place label 'Bond angle 109.5º' above-left of carbon around x = -0.82, y = 0.86. Bond-length guide lines: magenta dashed horizontal guides run rightward from top H level y = 1.08 and carbon level y = 0.00, starting just right of the vertical bond around x = 0.18 and ending near x = 1.72. Vertical double-headed magenta arrow at x = 1.72 from y = 0.00 to y = 1.08. Place text 'Bond length 109 pm' to the right at about x = 1.96, y = 0.54. FocusRepresentation should dim, outline, or slightly brighten the chosen panel, but should not replace the three-panel layout in the default view.
plan.notes: Render the central structural panel as screen-aligned 2D text, line, dashed-line, and filled-triangle geometry in an overlay-like group that remains front-on even when orbiting. Orbit3dModels should affect only the left and right molecular model groups, or should leave the center structural group billboarded and fixed so it never tilts in perspective. Use smooth sphere geometry with high specular highlights for the molecular models. For the space-filling panel, allow true sphere overlap and use soft lighting/ambient occlusion to make the central carbon barely visible through gaps; do not make the hydrogens transparent unless necessary. For the focus toggle, keep all three panels present; non-focused panels can be desaturated or dimmed to about 30 percent opacity rather than hidden. For click correspondence, picking any H or C-H bond should add a magenta or cyan highlight to the matching atom/bond in the other two panels, including a small glow or outline on the relevant structural label/line.
